problem:
Find the general solution to the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y=-x{y}^{3}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3{x}^{2}y={x}^{2}{y}^{-4}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that our equation is an instance of the Bernoulli differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+p(x)y=q(x){y}^{n}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
p(x)=-3{x}^{2},\,q(x)={x}^{2},\,n=-4.
$$

First, we multiply the differential equation by ${y}^{4},$ and we get

$$
{y}^{4}\frac{dy}{dx}-3{x}^{2}{y}^{5}={x}^{2}.\,\,(∗)
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z={y}^{1-n}={y}^{5}.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=5{y}^{4}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,{y}^{4}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

 

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z(x)$ as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{5}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-3{x}^{2}z={x}^{2}
$$

This differential equation is linear, so we can use the method of integrating factors. But first, we write the above equation in standard form:

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-15{x}^{2}z=5{x}^{2}
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)
$$

with

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x)=-15{x}^{2},\,Q(x)=5{x}^{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\int (-15{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{-5{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the standard form equation by $I(x)={e}^{-5{x}^{3}}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5{x}^{3}}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-15{x}^{2}z) & ={e}^{-5{x}^{3}}\cdot (5{x}^{2}) \\ {e}^{-5{x}^{3}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-15{x}^{2}z{e}^{-5{x}^{3}} & =5{x}^{2}{e}^{-5{x}^{3}} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(z{e}^{-5{x}^{3}}) & =5{x}^{2}{e}^{-5{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(z{e}^{-5{x}^{3}})\,\text{d}x & =\int 5{x}^{2}{e}^{-5{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\ z{e}^{-5{x}^{3}} & =-\frac{{e}^{-5{x}^{3}}}{3}+{C}_{1} \\ z & =\frac{C{e}^{5{x}^{3}}-1}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=3{C}_{1}.$

Finally, we determine $y(x)$ by writing $z={y}^{5}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{5}=\frac{C{e}^{5{x}^{3}}-1}{3}\,⇒\,y=\sqrt[5]{\frac{C{e}^{5{x}^{3}}-1}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
